assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, proglucagon processing, the active peptide form) leading to durable therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity is a rare case of basic discovery translating into a transformative, widely used class of drugs with effects well beyond glucose control. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are all very high.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 and its insulinotropic action), Drucker (biology and therapeutic concept, intestinotrophic roles) and Mojsov (identification of the biologically active GLP-1 form and its synthesis) are the strongest three from the supplied names. Knudsen is a major translational contributor in industry. Credit relative to others in the field who are not on the credited list is something I cannot resolve from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy and cardiometabolic outcomes are confirmed by large independent trials and by extensive real-world use; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among discoverers of the peptide, its physiology and its drug development, including contributors outside the credited list.
Long-term safety and the full breadth of benefits are still being characterized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a method for causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with light. Its originality and its influence across fields are exceptional, and it underpins a large fraction of modern circuit work.
assessment.attribution: The decisive steps are channelrhodopsin identification and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its demonstration as a neuronal tool (Boyden, Deisseroth). Credit is split among six credited names and a three-person cap forces hard choices. I propose Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel, while acknowledging that Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Widely and independently reproduced for about two decades; the method is mature and stable. Therapeutic uses (vision restoration) are early, but the discovery stands on its tool value.
uncertainties: Unresolved allocation among Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenböck and the three proposed names.
Whether recognition should emphasize the tool or the underlying microbial rhodopsin discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells have produced durable remissions in refractory leukemias and lymphomas and opened a new therapeutic modality. The concept, engineering and clinical proof are clear and the impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early chimeric-receptor and costimulation design), June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T in CLL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and clinical development). Other foundational contributors (for example Eshhar and others) are outside the supplied credit list, so a fair configuration is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent confirmation exist, so the clinical effect is established. Extension to solid tumors and toxicity management are still unresolved but do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept versus clinical translation.
Limited efficacy in solid tumors and long-term safety.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-based antisense correction of SMN2 splicing produced an effective therapy (nusinersen) for a previously devastating childhood disease. It is a clear proof that splicing modulation can be turned into medicine.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) form a coherent two-person configuration. Other contributors to SMN biology and to antisense chemistry are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated with years of follow-up and independent trials and approvals; timing is reasonable. Broader antisense field implications are still developing.
uncertainties: Breadth of credit for antisense chemistry versus the specific SMN2 application.
Overlap with SMN-gene discovery and other SMA therapies.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids opened a general platform for studying tissue renewal, disease and personalized models, built on identification of Lgr5 stem cells and long-term culture conditions. Originality and breadth are high.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem-cell and organoid work and Sato was central to the intestinal organoid culture system. This two-person configuration is plausible, though other organoid and stem-cell lineages (for example pluripotent-derived organoids) are outside the credit.
assessment.maturity: The method is widely adopted and reproduced. Clinical impact is still emerging, so recognition for the platform may be somewhat early relative to therapeutic evidence.
uncertainties: Relation to pluripotent-stem-cell organoid work and other culture systems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defined how cytosolic DNA is sensed by innate immunity, with implications for infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer. It is a mechanistically clear, conceptually original pathway.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and cGAMP identification) and Barber (STING) are the most defensible pair. The credited list also includes Sun, Wu and Ishikawa, who contributed to the discovery but are less likely to be recognized in a short prize configuration.
assessment.maturity: The pathway is extensively confirmed. Therapeutic exploitation is still in clinical development, so medical impact is not yet realized.
uncertainties: Allocation among STING discoverers and the cGAS group.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted inhibition of BCR-ABL turned chronic myeloid leukemia into a manageable disease and established the paradigm of oncogene-directed therapy. The lasting impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development), Lydon (discovery of the inhibitor chemistry) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) is a coherent set. Credit of the underlying BCR-ABL oncogene discovery (Rowley, Wong-Staal, others) is outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with more than two decades of clinical follow-up. Recognition is not premature and may be considered overdue from a timing standpoint, but the field has been well honored already.
uncertainties: Whether the oncogene discovery should be credited together with the drug.
Chemistry credit within the industry team.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The orexin/hypocretin discovery and its link to narcolepsy defined a neurochemical basis for sleep-wake regulation and opened drug development for sleep disorders. The discovery is clear and has had a strong disease-mechanism and therapeutic effect.
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa identified orexins and their receptors, while Mignot's canine genetics (hypocretin receptor 2) tied the system to narcolepsy. De Lecea and Kilduff made a parallel hypocretin discovery, so priority and allocation are genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed in animals and humans, with approved orexin receptor antagonists, so the finding is mature. The autoimmune etiology of narcolepsy is still not fully resolved.
uncertainties: Priority and credit split between the orexin and hypocretin groups.
Cause of orexin neuron loss in human narcolepsy remains unresolved.
